optimizedContext.value:
# SQLite Graph Store
## Rules
- `SQLiteGraphStore` implements `GraphStore` via `better-sqlite3`, preserving `code-graph:graph-store`. Stable id `sqlite`. Native binding resolution deferred until `open()`; `close()` idempotent.
- Every synchronous SQLite query, mutation, transaction, schema init, FTS, and backend maintenance runs in one persistent dedicated `node:worker_threads` worker per open store, never host event loop. One worker and one connection; no per-op workers or pooling. Concurrent `open()` or `close()` share in-flight lifecycle Promise.
- Worker owns `better-sqlite3` connection, prepared statements, transactions, schema, FTS, backend filesystem. Native handles and prepared statements MUST NOT cross boundary.
- Host/worker use typed structured-cloneable request, result, error, and progress DTOs with monotonic correlation ids. Functions, native objects, and class instances MUST NOT cross boundary.
- Worker FIFO serial queue so lifecycle, maintenance, reads, and mutations do not interleave.
- Host validates `maxPendingOperations >= 1`; default 256. Request beyond limit rejects immediately with `StoreOverloadError` without disturbing accepted work.
- `close()` rejects new work, drains accepted operations within `drainTimeoutMs` (default 5000 ms), requests worker-side database closure, force-terminates after graceful deadline. Unsettled requests reject `StoreWorkerError`. Await forced termination; MUST NOT claim hard wall-clock bound while native code executes.
- Runtime config crosses as serializable `SqliteRuntimeDescriptor`. Custom `modulePath` MAY select compatible binding. Absolute filesystem `modulePath` MUST convert to `file:` URL before dynamic `import()` so Windows drive-letter paths are not misread as URL schemes. Package specifiers and already-qualified `file:`, `data:`, and `node:` URLs pass through unchanged. Internal worker-path test overrides MUST NOT be public options.
- Unexpected worker error or exit faults store and rejects outstanding operations with `StoreWorkerError`. Recovery is explicit `close()` then `open()`; MUST NOT silently restart.
- If `close()` begins while `open()` is pending, shutdown owns final lifecycle state and `open()` MUST NOT subsequently publish `open`.
- Bulk indexing uses worker-side session `sessionId`. Only session start creates state; staging, commit, or rollback against missing or finalized session MUST reject. Host sessions enforce active, committing, rolling-back, and finished states and bind current store lifecycle generation.
- Progress callbacks observational. Callback failures isolated and MUST NOT abort worker operation or transaction.
- Closed-store recreation uses non-blocking host filesystem APIs for cleanup and storage-generation rotation.
- Batch symbol and relation queries are set-based worker operations. One batch call crosses boundary as one RPC, not one RPC per symbol or relation type. Incoming and outgoing relation lookup queries all requested symbol ids and relation types together. Large input sets split into deterministic bounded SQL parameter chunks inside worker so SQLite parameter limits cannot fail a valid traversal. Preserve abstract deterministic ordering and empty-input semantics.
- Filtered-impact uses parameterized SQL predicates for requested result types, symbol kinds, included workspaces, and excluded workspaces. Workspace predicates use persisted canonical workspace columns for files, specs, and logical symbols, or owning-file join for declaration symbols. Exclusions applied in SQL after inclusion normalization and take precedence.
- Constrain each impact frontier before materializing candidate rows. Result-type selection avoids hydrating unrequested file, symbol, or spec collections. Symbol-kind predicates belong to symbol query. Workspace predicates belong to every requested category query. Excluded rows MUST NOT cross from `SQLiteGraphDatabase` to `SQLiteGraphStore` for TypeScript post-filtering.
- Worker operation map defines serializable filtered-impact payload and result. `SQLiteGraphStore` sends normalized filter unchanged; worker dispatcher passes it unchanged to `SQLiteGraphDatabase`; database results return without widening. Generic worker client retains typed request, overload, lifecycle, and error behavior.
- Filtered reads stay bounded and deterministic. Empty inclusion lists omit inclusion predicate. Empty exclusion or kind lists omit their predicates. Duplicate filter values normalized before worker request. All dynamic values use bound parameters, not SQL interpolation.
- Exact batch lookups `getFilesByPaths`, `getDocumentsByPaths`, `getSpecsByIds`, `getSymbolsByIds`: one logical batch, one typed RPC. Set-based `path IN (...)` or `id IN (...)`. Deterministic bounded SQL parameter chunks. Dedupe repeated identities, omit unknown, preserve first requested-identity order. Empty input returns empty array without RPC.
- Root artifacts at project `configPath`. Graph dir `{configPath}/graph`; scratch `{configPath}/tmp`. Database, WAL, and shared-memory files live only under those dirs. Create required directories on demand.
- Built-in composition registers `sqlite` as sole built-in backend and selects it when no `graphStoreId`. Satisfies durable file, document, symbol, spec, relation, and metadata state; atomic mutations; full-text and identity-aware search for symbol, file, spec, and document discovery; bulk indexing and full re-index; structured traversal, references, coverage, impact, hotspots, search, and statistics. Unreadable graph after backend change recovers by full SQLite re-index.
- `recreate()` runs only after worker and database are closed. Reject while open. Remove graph persistence directory including SQLite companion files, rotate storage generation, return with no worker or database handle reopened.
- Open validation translates only known corruption and non-migratable schema to abstract typed recoverable storage-open error after closing partial database resources. Permission, configuration, native-runtime, and unrelated I/O errors propagate without recreation authority.
- Healthy forced reindex uses opened-store logical `clear()`. MUST NOT force by closing, deleting, reopening, or re-closing SQLite.
- When `recreate()` deletes SQLite database or WAL sidecars and deletion fails with `EPERM`, `EBUSY`, or `EACCES`, retry a bounded number of times then surface original error. MUST NOT delete a live `index.lock`. Lock held by a running index MUST survive recreation of database files.
- `clear()` executes one atomic logical-generation reset while worker remains open. Transaction removes physical graph rows, specs, relations, indexed-input observations, index-coverage rows, logical symbols and declarations, public and local bindings, reference and resolution facts, freshness latches, derivation metadata, and full-text index contents of cleared generation. After commit, indexing run MUST NOT treat a content hash, semantic row, or coverage record from cleared generation as authority to skip a discovered input. Failure rolls back to previously committed logical generation.
- Persist storage-generation sidecar compatible with `code-graph:graph-store` stale-detection. `graph/storage.epoch` acceptable. On `open()`, current generation observable to owning provider. Destructive recreation rotates generation so older open providers detect stale and must reopen.
- Adapter owns SQLite schema for files, symbols, specs, relations, full-text indexes, and store metadata: `File`, `Symbol`, `Spec`, `Meta`; relations matching `RelationType` including `EXTENDS`, `IMPLEMENTS`, `OVERRIDES`; derived columns such as normalized search text. Physical schema is adapter concern. Storage-agnostic consumers depend on `code-graph:graph-store`.
- Nodes: `File` with persisted source content for symbol snippets; `Symbol`; `Spec`; `Document`; `Meta`. `Document` columns: `path` (PK), `configRelativePath`, `contentHash`, `content`, `workspace`.
- Relations: `IMPORTS`, `DEFINES`, `CALLS`, `CONSTRUCTS`, `USES_TYPE`, `EXPORTS`, `DEPENDS_ON`, `COVERS_FILE`, `COVERS_SYMBOL`, `EXTENDS`, `IMPLEMENTS`, `OVERRIDES`. MAY use SQLite physical layout if observable `GraphStore` semantics preserved. `COVERS_SYMBOL` MUST preserve relation metadata so stale symbol-level links survive reload.
- `COVERS_SYMBOL` required target is a logical-symbol row. Physical declaration-occurrence symbol row alone MUST NOT satisfy that endpoint for newly projected coverage. Same committed transaction persists logical symbols before validating and inserting coverage relations. Valid logical coverage survives relation deduplication, reverse-coverage indexing, statistics, worker serialization, and subsequent `GraphStore` reads with target ID and metadata unchanged. Missing spec source or missing logical-symbol target rejected from committed relation set and reported through indexing diagnostic contract; not silently accepted or retargeted.
- FTS5 for symbol, spec, and document search. Keep `MATCH` for `searchSymbols()`, `searchSpecs()`, `searchDocuments()`. Search `Document` content and paths. Sanitize multi-token queries and join with `OR`. Expand raw tokens with shared specd/code-aware lexical policy before identity-aware ranking. Supplement FTS candidates with identity-derived candidates when FTS tokenization would miss a strong identity hit. Rank in SQL with explicit ordering columns, not BM25 weights alone.
- Exact canonical identity (Spec ID, Symbol Name/ID, Document Path) ranks first. Strong non-exact identity ahead of content-only: symbol declared-name equality when comment/body-only would rank higher; spec-id prefix, suffix, substring, and real component; document canonical-path or config-relative-path prefix, suffix, substring, and real component. Expanded-token coverage of selected identity fields ranks more matches above fewer. BM25 ranks remaining textual matches after identity preference.
- Order: exact canonical identity first; identity non-exact ahead of body-only, comment-only, content-only; exact token > prefix > suffix > arbitrary substring; real identity-component > arbitrary substring-only on same field; more expanded identity tokens outrank fewer when generic text relevance competes. Generic term frequency in spec/document body MUST NOT outrank a stronger spec-id, symbol-name, or document-path match.
- FTS tables: `symbol_fts` covers `Symbol.name` and `Symbol.comment`; `spec_fts` covers `Spec.title`, `Spec.description`, and `Spec.content`; `document_fts` covers `Document.path` and `Document.content`. MAY use stemming, weighted BM25, identity boost unions, or other SQLite ranking if abstract contract holds. Ranking via explicit SQL ordering such as computed rank columns or `CASE`. Discovery MAY combine `MATCH` with identity-derived candidates; MUST NOT replace FTS with plain whole-query `LIKE` only. Persisted `File` content for snippets SHALL NOT become a separate full-text searchable file category.
- Transactions execute entirely inside worker. A transaction MUST NOT span multiple host/worker round trips. Each atomic mutation, including `upsertFile()`, `removeFile()`, `upsertSpec()`, `removeSpec()`, and bulk commit, is one self-contained worker operation. Failure preserves previously committed graph state.
- Bulk indexing stages worker-side session in bounded chunks, not one repository-sized structured-clone payload. Commit makes complete session visible atomically in one SQLite transaction. Reference-fact chunks merge with earlier chunks from same session. Worker emits serializable progress for cleanup, files, documents, symbols, specs, reference facts, observations, relations, and search indexes. Host forwards them to optional observational callback. Prepared statements, temporary tables, and bounded SQL chunks MAY be used. Scratch artifacts remain under `{configPath}/tmp`.
- On open: execute current SQLite schema, verify or record schema version in persisted metadata, prepare FTS. Incompatible schema version MAY require destructive rebuild rather than incremental migration.
- WAL and shared-memory files under `{configPath}/graph` are SQLite implementation detail, not abstract `GraphStore` contract.
- Persist logical-symbol, declaration, member, symbol-space, binding, provenance, coverage, construct-range, and selection-range fields. Structured lookup columns indexed. Serialized canonical ids MUST NOT be parsed or substring-ranked for semantic lookup. Canonical ids stay unique external identities; backend-local integer row keys MAY join when provider-visible ids do not change.
- Maintain substring-capable source-content index and bounded short-query fallback. Reverse coverage and traversal batch reads use set-based predicates and deterministic ordering.
- Reference schema version `9`. Later schema-affecting change increments version exactly once. Incompatible data rejects ordinary reads. `graph index` rebuilds destructively, rotates `storage.epoch`, and rebuilds search indexes before readiness.
- Persist indexed-input observations, freshness latches, VCS evidence, and compact unchanged-file facts. One indexing run uses one transaction, set-based endpoint validation, bounded writes, one commit, and one semantic/content index rebuild.
## Constraints
- `SQLiteGraphStore` is an infrastructure adapter, not part of the abstract graph-store contract.
- `sqlite` is the stable backend id used to select this adapter from a multi-backend graph-store registry.
- SQLite file layout, FTS behavior, schema shape, and schema-version handling are defined here, not in `code-graph:graph-store`.
- All SQLite scratch files and persisted database artifacts are rooted under `configPath`.
- Storage-agnostic use cases and CLI commands MUST NOT depend on this spec unless they require SQLite-specific behavior.
